title: Joint Global-Local Representations via Relation-Entity Pair Encoding for Hyper-Relational Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: Hyper-relational knowledge graphs represent complex n-ary facts with qualifiers.

gap.claim: Existing methods can mix heterogeneous multi-hop evidence and fail to jointly model global inter-fact structure with local intra-fact semantics.

contributions.claim: GLoRE uses relation-entity pairs as the modeling primitive to preserve relation identity and within-fact roles during multi-hop aggregation.
The model constructs a weighted relation graph from co-occurrence statistics to refine relation representations in the pair encoder.
GLoRE combines global hypergraph propagation with local intra-fact self-attention and jointly optimizes both views through shared pair encoding.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art link prediction performance on JF17K, WikiPeople-, and WD50K, including 5-25% relative MRR improvements and first-ranked results across qualifier densities.
The authors report robustness to qualifier sparsity.
The authors state that code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hyper-relational knowledge graphs extend knowledge graphs with qualifiers for complex n-ary facts.
Prior methods may mix heterogeneous evidence and do not jointly capture global and local fact structure.
GLoRE encodes relation-entity pairs, uses relation co-occurrence priors, and combines global propagation with local attention.
Global and local views are jointly optimized through shared pair encoding.
The authors report improvements across three datasets and qualifier densities.

source_observation.claim: Relation-entity pair encoding is used to retain relation identity and within-fact roles.

interpretation.claim: Choosing a representation primitive that preserves role information may reduce ambiguity caused by heterogeneous aggregation.

application.claim: For structured data with typed roles, evaluate pair- or role-aware encodings before applying relation-agnostic aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design is beneficial outside the reported hyper-relational knowledge-graph setting.

unknowns: Training and inference costs are not reported.
Ablation results for the pair encoder, relation graph, global propagation, and local attention are not provided.
Dataset splits, baselines, and statistical uncertainty are not specified.
